phases.title: Make `break` and `skip` leave the loop instead of silently doing nothing
phases.finding: src/interpreter.rs:517-523 — `Statement::Break` and `Statement::Skip` each carry `// TODO: Implement proper control flow` and evaluate to `Ok(Value::Nothing)`. No loop consults them: `for each` (src/interpreter.rs:460), `repeat N times` (src/interpreter.rs:489) and `while` (src/interpreter.rs:505) all run their body to completion. Verified against the built binary: `for each i in [1,2,3] / if i is 2 then break end / say i / end` prints 1 2 3 and exits 0, and the same program with a `break` after `set n to n + 1` inside `repeat 5 times` still reports n = 5. SPEC.md:417-433 documents both statements with worked examples (`if i is 50 / break / end`), GRAMMAR.md:245-246 lists them, and src/lexer.rs:19-20 reserves the words while src/parser.rs:433-441 parses them — so the language accepts a program that compiles, runs, exits 0 and gives the WRONG ANSWER. Worse, two green tests pin the broken behaviour as correct: tests/test_lists.rb:108 `test "lists: break inside a loop does not truncate it"` asserts `expect total to be 10` where a working `break` at value 3 would make it 3, and tests/test_lists.rb:92 `test "lists: a conditional inside a loop does not disturb the iteration"` asserts `expect seen to be 4` where a working `skip` at value 2 would make it 3. A silent no-op that reports success is the most expensive class of defect this pipeline can ship.

There is no arm for `<`, `>`, `=` or `!`, so `if x > 10` fails with `LexerError: Unexpected character '>'`. Consequently TokenKind::Equal/NotEqual/Less/LessEqual/Greater/GreaterEqual (declared src/lexer.rs:137-144) are NEVER constructed by the lexer: `grep -rn 'TokenKind::Less\|TokenKind::Greater\|TokenKind::Equal\|TokenKind::NotEqual' src/*.rs` matches only src/parser.rs:1183-1258, i.e. the whole comparison arm block in parse_comparison is unreachable code. Consequence: the language has NO ordering comparison at all — `x > y`, `x < y`, `x == y`, `x != y` are all lex errors today.

phases.title: Show the compiler inside the REPL: `.bytecode` and `.asm`
phases.finding: The disassembler exists and the REPL cannot reach it: `bytecode::disassemble` at src/bytecode/disasm.rs:27 renders a `Chunk` to text, `rb dis` uses it from the CLI, and no REPL command calls it — so `what does this compile to` requires leaving the session, compiling to a file, and disassembling the artifact by hand. inscript ships exactly this pair (`.bytecode` compact listing, `.asm` full annotated assembly) because metaprogramming curiosity is a REPL-native question; redblue's S1/S2 ladder makes it load-bearing here too, since the REPL is where users first meet the bytecode their code becomes.
phases.goal: Add `.bytecode <expr>` (compact instruction listing) and `.asm <expr>` (annotated assembly with constants and spans) that compile the expression through the same frontend the session executes and render through the existing disassembler. Read-only: nothing is written to disk and the session VM is untouched.
accept: `.bytecode say 1` prints an instruction listing containing a constant load and asserts the version line matches `FORMAT_VERSION` (derived, not hardcoded)
`.asm` on the same input prints strictly more than `.bytecode` (constants table + spans), asserted by comparing line counts on one fixed input
an expression that fails to compile reports the compile error instead of disassembling nothing — `.bytecode might fail 1 +` names the parser error rather than printing an empty listing
both commands agree with `rb dis` on the same source byte-for-byte modulo the REPL header (one test compiles a temp file both ways and diffs)
edge_* tests cover `.bytecode` with no argument, a 2000-line generated program (renders without hanging), and non-UTF8-safe constant content (never panics on display)

phases.title: Make REPL errors point at the code: source context through the color system
phases.finding: REPL errors discard the rendering the language already owns: `execute_code` at src/repl/mod.rs:407 prints `Error: {}` via `Display`, while `Error::render()` at src/error.rs:105 builds the full diagnostic — label, message, `--> location`, source line, and caret gutter (error.rs:105-125). Every REPL failure therefore shows less than `rb run` shows for the same program: no source line, no caret, no span, no color. inscript prints the offending line plus caret in-REPL for exactly this reason; a REPL that hides locations teaches users to leave it when something breaks.
phases.goal: Route REPL error output through `Error::render()` with the session's current buffer as the source, colored through the phase-053 system (label + location in the error color, source line plain, caret line highlighted). The message text stays identical — color wraps it, never rewrites it.
accept: typing `say nosuchvar` prints the source line `say nosuchvar` plus a caret line under `nosuchvar` — asserted on the rendered string with colors stripped, so the test is immune to palette changes
the same error through `rb run` and through the REPL carries the same `--> line:column` location (one test runs both and diffs the location line)
with colors forced off the REPL error is byte-identical to `Error::render()` output for the same input (no REPL-specific reformatting hiding behind the colors)

both engines agree: an error raised under the bytecode VM path renders with the same location as under the tree-walker (the session executes through one engine; the test runs the other and compares locations)

edge_* tests cover a multiline-block error (caret points into the right buffered line, not line 1), an error with no span (renders message-only, never panics on a missing location), and a 500-character line (caret alignment survives wide content)

phases.title: Export sessions and complete file paths: `.export` plus TAB for `:load`/`:save`
phases.finding: A session cannot leave the terminal except as raw history: no `.export` command exists in commands.rs (verified absent), so sharing a session means copy-pasting terminal scrollback, colors and prompts included. And the file-argument commands (`:load`, `:save`, `:run`, `:restore`) take paths the editor cannot complete — the completer at src/repl/completer.rs handles `:`/`.` command sigils only (completer.rs:297-302) with no path handling at all, so every filename is typed blind. Ipp completes paths for `.load`/`.save`/`.cd`/`.ls`/`.edit` including directory traversal; inscript persists sessions to `.ins` files.
phases.goal: Add `.export [file]` writing the session (inputs, outputs, errors) as Markdown with Redblue fences and no escape codes, defaulting to stdout when no file is given; and teach TAB to complete filesystem paths after the four file-argument commands, with directories offered with a trailing separator.
accept: `.export` to stdout of a two-line session produces Markdown with exactly two ` ```redblue ` fences and the outputs as text blocks — asserted structurally, with all escapes stripped first so color codes can never leak into an export
TAB after `:load ` offers files in the current directory and TAB after `:load sr` narrows to the `src/` directory with its trailing separator
TAB path completion never escapes the argument: completing inside `say "a` does not offer files (the path logic fires only after the four file commands)
round-trip: `.export session.md` then a fresh session reads the fenced blocks back and reproduces the outputs (pinned on a fixed two-line session, not on wall time)

edge_* tests cover `.export` to an unwritable path (clean error naming the path), TAB after `:load ` in an empty directory (no candidates, no crash), and a filename containing a space (offered quoted or escaped, never split)

phases.title: Complete after the dot, edit in `$EDITOR`, and teach newcomers: member completion, `.edit`, `:tutorial`
phases.finding: Three discoverability gaps share one root — the REPL knows things it will not offer. Member completion: typing `json.` offers nothing although `json_parse`/`json_stringify` are registered builtins and `.doc json` (phase-056) lists them; the completer has no dot handling (verified above). External editing: a 50-line block can only be typed or `:load`ed, because no `.edit` command exists (verified absent) — both Ipp and inscript shell out to `$EDITOR` for exactly this. Guided entry: no `:tutorial`/`:examples` exists (verified absent) although `:example` does, so a newcomer gets one static dump rather than a walkthrough; Ipp's `.tutorial` and inscript's guided tour are the model.
phases.goal: Complete member names after a module dot (`json.` offers `parse`/`stringify`); add `.edit` opening `$EDITOR` on the current buffer (or a scratch file) and executing the result on save; add `:tutorial` as a short guided tour ending in `:examples`. Each is independently useful and independently tested. A `.hint` command prints the current tutorial lesson's hint, and typing `(` after a callable name shows its signature inline (the `(` row of Ipp's own help table).
accept: `json.` + TAB offers `parse` and `stringify` and exactly the members the registry holds for `json` (expectation derived from `builtins()`, so registry and completion cannot drift); `nosuchmodule.` + TAB offers nothing and does not error
`.edit` with `EDITOR=true` round-trips the multiline buffer through the editor and executes what comes back (pinned with a script editor, never a real TTY editor)
`:tutorial` prints a numbered multi-step tour whose final step names `:examples`, and every snippet it shows executes cleanly when pasted (a test runs each fenced block through the session)
member completion and file-path completion do not fight: `json.` completes members while `:load j` completes paths, each gated on its own context

edge_* tests cover `.edit` with `EDITOR` unset (clean error naming the variable, session buffer preserved), TAB after a bare `.` (offers module names), and `:tutorial` with colors forced off (numbering intact, no escapes)
`.hint` outside the tutorial names `:tutorial` instead of failing blank; typing `(` after `split` surfaces its separator form before the call runs (asserted through the signature hook, not a TTY)

phases.title: Open a debug sub-REPL: `.debug` with `.watch`, `.stack` and `.locals`
phases.finding: Debugging means leaving the REPL: no `.debug` command exists in commands.rs (verified absent along with `watch`, `stack`, `locals`), so inspecting a failing program means re-running it under `rb run` with `say` statements added — the print-debugging the REPL exists to obsolete. Both Ipp (debug REPL with `.watch`/`.locals`/`.stack`, VM-debug wired through the highlighted session) and inscript (frame debugger with `.watch`/`.stack`/`.locals`/`.globals`/`.type`, plus REPL-polish tests asserting each handler exists) treat an in-session debugger as REPL work, not VM work.
phases.goal: Add `.debug <expr|file>` entering a sub-REPL that evaluates with tracing on: `.watch <expr>` re-evaluates an expression after every step and reports changes, `.stack` lists the live call frames, `.locals` lists frame bindings, and exiting returns to the parent session with its state untouched. Scope is observe-only: no breakpoints, no stepping primitives — those are their own phase if the debugger proves its worth.
accept: `.debug` on a three-deep call chain followed by `.stack` names all three functions in order (asserted through the sub-REPL driver, not a TTY)
`.watch x` reports exactly the steps where `x` changed value across a loop, and stays silent on steps where it did not (a test counts the report lines)
`.locals` inside a function frame shows parameters and locals and nothing from the caller's frame (frame isolation asserted, not assumed)
exiting the sub-REPL leaves the parent session byte-identical to before `.debug` ran (bindings, history and last-result all diffed, not eyeballed)

edge_* tests cover `.debug` with no argument, `.watch` with an expression that fails (reports the error once per step without aborting the session), and `.stack` with no live frames (empty, named as such, never a panic)

phases.title: Print values three ways: `.pretty`, `.json`, `.table`
phases.finding: Every value the REPL prints goes through one shape: `println!("= {}", value)` at src/repl/mod.rs:402, the single-line `Display`. A 200-element list, a nested record, and a table-shaped list of records all print as one unreadable line, and there is no way to ask for JSON or columns — `pretty`, `json` and `table` are all absent from src/repl/commands.rs (verified by name loop). Ipp ships exactly this trio (`.pretty`, `.json` viewer, `.table <var>` for lists of dicts) because data inspection is REPL-native work; `:inspect` answers for one variable but formats nothing.
phases.goal: Add `.pretty <expr>` (indented structure), `.json <expr>` (JSON rendering of the value), and `.table <list>` (list-of-records as aligned columns). All three reuse the value's existing rendering and only reflow it; none executes anything beyond evaluating its argument.
accept: `.pretty` on a nested record indents one level per depth and the output parses back to an equal value (round-trip asserted, not eyeballed)
`.json` output is valid JSON per `serde_json` (already a dev-dependency) on numbers, texts, lists, records and `nothing` (as `null`)
`.table` on a list of records with a shared key set aligns columns and names the keys once in a header row; ragged rows (missing keys) render empty cells rather than erroring
every new command appears in `:help` (same help-completeness test pattern as phase-056)

edge_* tests cover `.pretty` of a 10-deep nesting (terminates, bounded width), `.json` of a non-finite number (refused or null per the SPEC rule, never `NaN` literal), and `.table` of an empty list (header-only or a named empty, never a panic)

phases.title: Close the file loop: `.reload`, `.format`, and format-on-enter
phases.finding: The file workflow is write-only in the wrong direction: `:load`/`:run` read files in, but nothing re-reads one (`reload` absent from commands.rs, verified), and nothing formats what was typed — `format` is absent too, although `src/formatter.rs` implements `rbfmt` and `rb format` ships it from the CLI. So a session that iterates on a file re-types `:load` by hand and pastes unformatted code it can never normalize without leaving. Ipp's `.format` goes one step further: auto-format on Enter as a toggle, so pasted code normalizes itself line by line.
phases.goal: Add `.reload` (re-runs the last `:load`ed/`:run` file, erroring cleanly when there is none), `.format` (pretty-prints the current multiline buffer through `rbfmt` without executing it), and a `.format on|off` toggle that formats each entered line before execution. All three reuse the existing formatter; none changes what the formatter accepts.
accept: `.reload` after `:load` re-executes the file and reproduces its output; `.reload` with no file loaded is a clean error naming `:load`, not a panic on missing state
`.format` on an ugly-but-valid buffer prints the canonical form and leaves the buffer unexecuted (asserted: bindings unchanged after `.format`)
with the toggle on, entering `set   x    to   1` executes `set x to 1` (proved by the binding existing afterwards); with it off, the line executes verbatim
a buffer the formatter rejects is executed (or refused) exactly as with the toggle off — the toggle never converts a formatter error into a silent acceptance

edge_* tests cover `.reload` after the file was deleted since loading (clean IO error with the path), `.format` on an empty buffer (no-op, no crash), and toggle state surviving `:reset` (it is a session preference, asserted on both sides)

phases.title: Let users extend the REPL: `.alias` and `.macro`
phases.finding: `alias` and `macro` are both absent from src/repl/commands.rs (verified), so every repeated workflow is retyped in full: there is no short name for a long command and no way to record a sequence once and replay it. Ipp ships both (`.alias n cmd`, `.macro` define/list) for exactly this reason. The machinery is small — the command table already parses aliases (`:hist`, `:v`, `:f` work today), so user aliases are the same table with user rows — but the absence forces repetition onto every session.
phases.goal: Add `.alias <name> <command>` (user-named command shortcuts, listed in `:help`, shadowing nothing built in) and `.macro` (record the session's lines between start/stop, replay them by name, list them). Aliases and macros live in the session and die with it unless `:save`d; a name colliding with a builtin is refused.
accept: `.alias ll :vars` makes `ll` behave exactly as `:vars` (outputs diffed, not eyeballed); `.alias :vars :help` is refused naming the collision with a builtin
a recorded macro of three lines replays all three in order with identical outputs (asserted by diffing two transcripts); `.macro` with no recording in progress is a clean usage error
aliases and macros appear in `:help` output under their own section (help-completeness pattern), and TAB completes user macro names as well as builtins
`:save` persists aliases and macros and `:restore` brings them back (round-trip asserted on a session carrying one of each)

edge_* tests cover an alias whose value is another alias (resolves, exactly one level, no infinite loop on `.alias a b` + `.alias b a` — refused as a cycle), a macro recording across `:reset` (recording survives, bindings do not), and `.alias` with no arguments (lists current aliases, empty list named as such)

phases.title: Settle engine arguments with evidence: `.compare` runs both engines
phases.finding: `compare` is absent from commands.rs (verified), so the two engines can only be compared by leaving the REPL: redblue owns a tree-walking VM (`self.vm.run`, src/repl/mod.rs:443-451 — the only engine the session uses) and a bytecode VM, and today `do they agree on this program` means compiling to a file and running `rb vm` by hand. The differential-test suite proves agreement in CI, but the curious user at the prompt has no such tool. Ipp's `.compare a b` compares two expressions; redblue's sharper question is one expression on two engines.
phases.goal: Add `.compare <expr>` compiling and running the expression on the tree-walker and the bytecode VM, printing both values side by side and saying AGREE or naming the difference. Read-only: neither engine's state may leak into the session (both run on clones), and a compile failure reports instead of comparing nothing.
accept: `.compare 1 + 2` prints both values and AGREE (asserted on the verdict word, not the values alone, so a test cannot pass by printing one side twice)

a construct the engines genuinely differ on (seeded from the differential corpus, e.g. a known edge file) prints DIFFER with both values named — the command must be able to fail, so the happy path alone does not pin it
running `.compare` leaves the session VM untouched (bindings before and after diffed — the comparison clones state, never borrows it)
an expression that fails to compile reports the compile error once rather than comparing two absences

edge_* tests cover `.compare` with no argument, `.compare` on a program with side effects (`say` runs exactly once per engine — asserted on output line counts, so effects are never doubled into the session), and a 10KB generated program (both engines finish, verdict printed)

phases.title: Give the session a memory: `.checkpoint`, `.restore`, `.undo`, `.redo`, `.sessions`
phases.finding: Session state has exactly one granularity — everything (`:save`/`:restore` whole-session files, mod.rs:594-633) or nothing — and `checkpoint`, `restore`, `undo`, `redo` and `sessions` are all absent from commands.rs (verified; the `:restore` hit is the file command, a different feature). So there is no way to try something destructive and step back: a `set` that clobbers a binding, an import that shadows, a 200-line paste that half-fails — all permanent until `:reset` wipes everything. Ipp ships `.checkpoint`/`.restore` (environment snapshots), `.undo`/`.redo` (single-step), and `.sessions` (listing) as one family; redblue needs the family, named to never collide with the file commands.
phases.goal: Add named in-memory snapshots (`.checkpoint <name>`, `.restore <name>`, `.sessions` listing them) plus single-step `.undo`/`.redo` over binding changes. Snapshots capture bindings, last-result and history position; they are session-local (never files, never committed) and die with the session. Names colliding with file-restore semantics are refused by the help text, which states the file/memory split once.
accept: `.checkpoint a`, clobber a binding, `.restore a` brings the old value back exactly (asserted on the value, and on `_` last-result too — the snapshot is the whole state, not just the map)
`.undo` after one `set` removes exactly that binding and `.redo` brings it back; `.undo` with an empty undo stack is a named empty, never a panic
`.sessions` lists checkpoint names in creation order with the current one marked; with no checkpoints it says so rather than printing a blank table
`:save`/`:restore` file semantics are untouched (the existing save/restore tests pass unmodified) and the help text states the file-vs-memory split in one sentence (asserted by a help-text test)

edge_* tests cover `.restore` of an unknown name, `.checkpoint` with a duplicate name (refused, old one kept — never silent overwrite), undo across 50 bindings (stack bounded, oldest dropped with a notice, never unbounded growth), and `.redo` after a new change (redo stack cleared, stated in the message)

phases.title: Talk to the shell without leaving: `!cmd`, `.pipe`, `.cd`, `.pwd`, `.ls`
phases.finding: The session is sealed from its own machine: `pipe`, `cd`, `pwd` and `ls` are all absent from commands.rs (verified), and no `!` shell escape exists — so running a file listing, checking a path, or sending output through a pager means suspending the REPL and opening a second terminal. Ipp ships `! <cmd>` (shell execute), `.pipe <cmd>` (output to shell), and `.cd`/`.ls`/`.pwd` (navigation) as REPL-native because file arguments (`:load`, `:save`, `:export`) are typed blind without them — which phase-060's path completion only half fixes: completion needs a visible directory.
phases.goal: Add `!cmd` (run a shell command, show its output and exit code), `.pipe <cmd>` (send the last result/output through a shell command), and `.cd`/`.pwd`/`.ls` (session working directory affecting all relative file arguments). Shell features are host-only and labeled as such; on targets without a shell they refuse cleanly rather than failing obscurely.
accept: `!echo hi` prints `hi` and a zero exit (asserted on both, so a silent failure cannot pass); a failing command prints its exit code rather than the REPL's error format
`.pipe` sends the last `_` value to the command's stdin (pinned with a stdin-echo command, proving the direction); with no last result it says so instead of piping emptiness
`.cd` into a temp dir makes `:load` resolve there (proved by loading a file by bare name after `.cd`), and `.pwd` prints the session directory distinctly from the process directory
`.ls` lists the session directory with directories marked (trailing separator, matching the phase-060 completion contract so the two agree)

edge_* tests cover `!` with an empty command (usage, no shell spawned), `.pipe` to a command that fails (exit code surfaces, session survives), `.cd` to a missing directory (clean error naming the path, directory unchanged), and a 1MB piped payload (streams, never loads whole into a string twice)

phases.title: Find things without leaving: `.search` across docs, history, bindings and help
phases.finding: `search` is absent from commands.rs (verified), so every lookup is a different tool: builtin docs need `.doc` with the exact name, history needs eyeballing `:history`, session bindings need eyeballing `:vars`, and help needs reading end to end. `which builtin does string splitting` has no answer inside the session although the data is all there — the registry, the help table, the history buffer and the session map. Ipp's `.search <kw>` searches builtin documentation in one place for exactly this reason.
phases.goal: Add `.search <keyword>` ranking matches across four sources — builtin docs/signatures, `:help` text, session bindings, and history — with the source labeled per hit. Read-only: searching never executes, binds, or reorders anything.
accept: `.search split` finds the `split` builtin, the phase-056 `.sighelp` entry if present, and any history line mentioning it, each labeled with its source (asserted per-source, so a source going dark fails the test)
`.search` ranks exact-name matches above substring matches (pinned on a fixed query with both kinds present)
`.search` with no argument prints usage rather than dumping every source (a full dump is a denial-of-patience, not a search)
history matches show their history numbers so the hit can be re-run with `!!`-style recall or by number

edge_* tests cover a keyword matching nothing (named empty per source, never a blank page), a 1-character keyword (refused as too short with the minimum stated, so single letters never dump the registry), and regex-significant characters in the keyword (treated literally, never as a pattern)

phases.title: Weigh the session: `.mem` and `.profile`
phases.finding: `mem` and `profile` are both absent from commands.rs (verified): a session that grows strange — a runaway history, a binding holding megabytes, a line that takes seconds — offers no instrument except leaving and guessing. Ipp's `.mem` (memory usage) and `.profile` (last-command profile) exist because interactive performance questions are REPL-native; redblue's `.time`/`.bench` (phase-057) time expressions but say nothing about where the session's own weight lives.
phases.goal: Add `.mem` (bindings count + largest bindings by size, history entries + bytes, VM heap estimate, each labeled) and `.profile` (per-line timing breakdown of the last multiline block, slowest first). Both observe: measuring must not mutate bindings, history, or last-result.
accept: `.mem` after binding a 10KB text reports it as the largest binding with its byte size within 10% (approximate honestly — the test asserts the ranking and the order of magnitude, never an exact allocator number)
`.profile` on a three-line block attributes time per line summing to within 20% of the block total (asserted on the arithmetic relationship, which holds regardless of machine speed)
running `.mem` twice in a row changes neither the binding count nor `_` (observation is side-effect-free, proved by diffing full session state around the command)
sizes render in human units (B/KB/MB) with the raw bytes in parentheses, so small and large sessions read alike

edge_* tests cover `.mem` on a fresh session (zeros named as zeros, never blank), `.profile` with no previous block (names `:history`-visible absence instead of profiling nothing), and a binding holding a 5MB text (reported, session stays responsive — no full clone into the report)

phases.title: Map the whole environment: `.env`, `.types`, `.dir`, `.typehints`
phases.finding: `env`, `types`, `dir` and `typehints` are all absent from commands.rs (verified): `.vars` lists names, `.type` (phase-056) answers for one expression, and between them lies everything structural — the full binding tree, every record/object shape in the session, every field of one value, every session variable's type at a glance. inscript's `.env` (full environment tree) and `.types` (struct/enum listing) plus Ipp's `.dir` (object attributes) and `.typehints` (variable types) are that middle layer, and redblue's records/objects make it more necessary here, not less.
phases.goal: Add `.env` (binding tree: session vars, imports, module members, each with kind), `.types` (every distinct record/object shape in the session with field names), `.dir <value>` (fields + methods of one value), and `.typehints` (every session variable with its current type in one table). All four derive from live session state — hardcoded expectations are forbidden; the tests build state then assert the listing reflects it.
accept: after `set r to {a: 1, b: "x"}`, `.types` names a shape with fields `a, b` and `.dir r` lists both fields with their values' kinds
`.env` shows a session var, an imported module member, and a builtin under three labeled sections (asserted per-section, so a silent source regresses loudly)
`.typehints` lists every session variable with its type; rebinding a var to another type updates its row (proved by binding, listing, rebinding, listing)
importing a module adds its section to `.env` without duplicating session vars (asserted by counting rows before and after the import)

edge_* tests cover `.env` on a fresh session (builtins section present, session section named-empty), `.dir` on a non-record (fields section absent, methods/kind still shown), `.types` with no records bound (named empty), and a record with 100 fields (renders complete, no truncation without notice)

phases.title: Let the session switch engines: `.vm` toggles tree-walker and bytecode VM
phases.finding: The session runs one engine and cannot meet the other: `run_program` at src/repl/mod.rs:443-451 calls `self.vm.run(program)` unconditionally, and no `BytecodeVm`, engine flag, or toggle exists anywhere in src/repl/ (verified by grep) — although the language ships two engines and phase-066's `.compare` will prove they can disagree. Both Ipp (`.vm interpreter/vm`, shown in the banner with a switch hint) and inscript (`.vm` toggle) treat engine choice as session state, because `which engine am I talking to` is the first question behind every behavioral surprise.
phases.goal: Add `.vm [walker|bytecode]` showing the current engine or switching it, with the banner and prompt naming the engine at all times. Bindings survive the switch (both engines read the same session state); history and last-result are engine-independent and untouched. The default stays the tree-walker: the documented language semantics.
accept: `.vm` with no argument names the current engine; `.vm bytecode` then `say 1+1` prints `3` through the bytecode VM (proved by an engine-marker in a test hook, not by trusting the prompt text)
bindings survive both directions (`set x to 9`, switch, `say x` prints `9`, switch back, still `9` — asserted on values, so state is shared and never re-seeded)
an engine-specific divergence is reported with the engine named (seeded from a differential-corpus edge both engines treat differently, so the test cannot pass on one engine twice)
`.vm` with a third engine name is refused listing the two valid ones; the prompt shows the engine after every switch without needing `:help` to confirm

edge_* tests cover switching mid-multiline-block (block preserved, engine applies at execution), `.vm` inside a `:save`d session (engine choice persists through save/restore), and rapid double-switch (idempotent, session identical)

phases.title: Measure before optimizing: a benchmark harness with a checked-in baseline
phases.finding: Redblue has no benchmark harness at all: no `benches/` or `benchmarks/` directory exists, `Cargo.toml` names no criterion/divan dependency, and no BASELINE file records how fast anything is. Ipp ships `benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py` plus a checked-in `BENCHMARKS.md` table (fibonacci, prime counting, mandelbrot, string concat across interpreter/VM/Python/Node) for exactly this reason — and phase-022's 29.0s-to-3.5s speedup claim had nowhere to live except a FINDINGS paragraph, so no later phase can tell whether it regressed. Performance work without a harness is unmeasurable by construction.
phases.goal: Add a benchmark harness (named workloads: fibonacci, prime counting, string concat, lex-heavy compile) that prints a timing table and records it in a checked-in `BENCH.md`, with every workload asserting the CORRECTNESS of its output (fib(20)==6765 etc. — deterministic, never flaky). Wall time is printed and recorded but never asserted: timing assertions are flakes wearing a gate's clothes.
accept: four named workloads run to completion and print one table with per-workload wall time (asserted present in output, never asserted exact)

every workload asserts its computed answer against a literal (fib(20) is 6765, the prime count is exact, the concat is exact) — a benchmark that computes the wrong answer fast is the failure this pins
`BENCH.md` is checked in with the measured table from the landing machine plus its hardware note, and a test asserts the file exists and names all four workloads (content may move, coverage may not)
the harness runs outside the `cargo test` gate path (it measures, it does not gate) while its correctness assertions run inside it — one mechanism never serves both masters

edge_* tests cover an empty workload name (clean usage error listing the four), a workload given a size of zero (completes, answer asserted trivially true), and a 60-second budget the harness enforces itself (a hung workload fails loudly instead of hanging CI)

phases.title: Hash the self-hosted compiler's intern table instead of scanning it
phases.finding: `to intern(raw)` at bootstrap/compiler.rb:2285 walks the whole table on every name emitted: `while intern_i < length(G_INTERN)` with `if G_INTERN[intern_i].k is raw` at :2290-2291, returning the index or appending. Every name in the program — via `emit_name` at :2310, called for modules (:2473, :2480), objects (:2529, :2532) and every other named emit — pays a scan of the 1000+-entry table, which phase-022 FINDINGS section 4 measured as most of codegen's remaining 6 seconds and explicitly deferred: `A hash map in the language would fix it; that is a language change and belongs in its own phase.` That phase is this one. The fixed-point suite (stage1.rbc == stage2.rbc byte for byte) guards the change: a faster compiler that emits different bytes is a failure, not an optimization.
phases.goal: Replace the linear `G_INTERN` scan with a hash lookup in the language (a name-to-index record probed by a string hash the language can compute), keeping every emitted byte identical. Codegen time on `bootstrap/compiler.rb` must drop measurably on the phase-073 harness; the fixed point must hold exactly.
accept: `edge_the_self_hosted_compiler_compiles_itself_byte_identically` passes unmodified — the optimization changes zero emitted bytes, proved by the standing fixed point rather than a new assertion

codegen wall time on `bootstrap/compiler.rb` drops by at least 25% measured by the phase-073 harness on the same machine back-to-back (recorded in REPORT.md with both numbers, not asserted in a test — machine variance is real)
interning the same name twice returns the same index without growing the table (a test interns 1000 repetitions and asserts table growth of exactly the distinct count)
hash collisions resolve correctly: a test interns two names engineered to share a bucket and asserts both retrieve their own index (the test constructs the collision rather than hoping for one)

edge_* tests cover interning the empty string, a 10KB name (hashes, never truncates), and interning during a self-compile (the fixed point covers it, plus one direct test asserting `stage2` bytes equal `stage1` bytes for a name-heavy fixture file)

phases.title: Teach the language server navigation: goto-definition, references, completion
phases.finding: src/lsp.rs answers questions about a file but cannot move inside it: its public surface is `diagnostics`, `diagnostics_json`, `keyword_pattern`, `escape_json` and `textmate_grammar` (lsp.rs:44-233) — diagnostics plus editor assets, no navigation. Ipp's `lsp/server.py` ships `goto_definition` (:113), `find_references` (:131) and `get_completions` (:149) with enhanced context awareness, because diagnostics without navigation is a linter with a wire protocol: the editor can underline the error but cannot jump to the definition. Phase-017 scaffolded the server; this is the first capability beyond scaffolding.
phases.goal: Add goto-definition (name at position to its binding span), find-references (all uses of the binding at position), and completion (keywords + builtins + in-scope names at position) to `src/lsp.rs`, each as a pure function over source text returning JSON the existing `diagnostics_json` shape extends. No server loop changes: capabilities first, transport later.
accept: goto-definition on a `set` variable's use returns its declaration span (line + column asserted exactly on a fixed fixture — positions are deterministic, never approximate)
find-references on one binding returns every use and no use of a same-named binding in another scope (shadowing fixture: inner `x` and outer `x` distinguished)
completion at an empty prefix offers keywords, builtins and in-scope session names; completion inside a string literal offers nothing (context awareness asserted, not just prefix matching)
all three return the existing `{line, column, ...}` JSON shape extended per capability, and malformed positions (line 0, column past end) are clean errors, never panics

edge_* tests cover goto-definition on a builtin (resolves to the builtin registry, not a file span), references to an imported module member (spans the import, not the definition site), completion at EOF without trailing newline, and a 5000-line file (all three answer in under a second — a benchmark assertion, not a wall-time gate)

phases.title: Scaffold projects: `rb new`, root discovery, and a project-aware `rb test`
phases.finding: Redblue has files but no projects: `rb test [path]` at src/lib.rs:127 runs one path or the suite, and nothing discovers a project root, creates one, or runs a project's own tests — while Ipp ships `ipp new <name>` (scaffold.py: layout + `ipp.toml` + `src/` + `tests/`) with walk-up root discovery (`find_project_root` in project.py) as the normal way to start. Depending on phase-044 is load-bearing, not ceremonial: 044 owns the manifest schema (name/version/deps), so this phase reads that schema and must add no version/deps fields of its own — inventing a second schema here is exactly the collision the dependency exists to prevent.
phases.goal: Add `rb new <name>` (layout + entry + tests dir + manifest in 044's schema), walk-up project-root discovery used by every file-argument command, and bare `rb test` running the discovered project's `tests/` directory. If phase-044's schema is not yet on main, this phase waits rather than inventing: the dependency says so.
accept: `rb new hello` creates the layout and `rb test` inside it runs the scaffolded tests green (end-to-end asserted on a temp dir, never the real tree)
`rb new` into an existing non-empty directory is refused naming the directory (never merges into occupied ground, never overwrites)
root discovery walks up: running `rb test` from a nested `src/` finds the project root and runs the root's tests (pinned on a three-deep fixture tree)
`rb test <path>` behavior is byte-identical to today (the existing test-runner tests pass unmodified — discovery only fills in the path when none is given)
the manifest written by `rb new` validates against phase-044's schema test unchanged (no new fields, no renamed fields — asserted by running 044's own schema test over the fresh file)

edge_* tests cover `rb new` with no name, with a name containing a path separator (refused, stays in cwd), `rb test` outside any project (clean error naming `rb new`, exit non-zero), and a project whose manifest is malformed (names the file and the offending line)

phases.title: Finish the list surface: `sort`, `reverse`, `zip`, `enumerate`, `filter`, `reduce`
phases.finding: The list surface stops halfway: `map` works (with `list_map`), `pop`/`shift` were wired in phase-032, and `filter`, `reduce`, `sort`, `reverse`, `zip` and `enumerate` are all missing — `filter`/`reduce`/`list_map` sit in `tests/stdlib_module_docs_test.rs::KNOWN_GAPS` explicitly deferred as higher-order work needing a walker's captured scopes. inscript ships map/filter/reduce/zip/enumerate/sort/reverse as core builtins because list transformation is everyday code, not a special occasion. The first-order four are pure functions on values; the higher-order two follow the `map_builtin` precedent in both VMs.
phases.goal: Implement `sort`, `reverse`, `zip`, `enumerate` as pure builtins and `filter`, `reduce` as higher-order builtins in both engines next to `map_builtin`, then remove all six from `KNOWN_GAPS` (which is what makes the surface test cover them instead of excusing them). Dotted module spellings (`list.sort`) resolve through the existing `stdlib::resolve` path.
accept: `sort`, `reverse`, `zip` and `enumerate` answer on both engines with identical output (one differential test per builtin across the two VMs, values diffed not eyeballed)
`filter` and `reduce` call Redblue functions per element in order on both engines, proved by a side-effect-counting function (counter asserted exact — order and count both pinned)
all six are removed from `KNOWN_GAPS`, so the registry-walk test now covers them; the remaining gaps stay listed with their reasons (the list shrinks, never silently)
`sort` is stable (equal elements keep their order — asserted on records sharing a key) and refuses mixed-type lists by name rather than ordering across kinds

edge_* tests cover `sort` of an empty list, `zip` of unequal lengths (stops at the shorter, stated in SPEC), `enumerate` start index, `reduce` on an empty list with and without an initial value (the two cases differ and both are pinned), and `filter` whose function fails mid-list (the failure aborts with the error, partial results never surface)

phases.title: Make the checkpoint ancestry in redblue main detectable instead of a comment
phases.finding: rbops/dispatch.sh:442-447 admits it in prose and nothing measures it, so the number can only grow silently: 'six of them are in redblue's history today, carrying unreviewed code.' Measured this audit: `git -C redblue log --oneline main | grep checkpoint` prints 4 lines - 7fdea15 and 074c95e `rbops: phase-019 checkpoint`, 563a351 `rbops: phase-018 checkpoint`, 286fccd `rbops: phase-016 checkpoint` - and `git -C redblue log --oneline main | grep -c "Merge remote-tracking branch"` prints 4, the real `git merge` commits that put them there (e97983a, d664d3c, 2179034, 255816e). rbops/dispatch.sh:439-486 now resumes with `git merge --squash`, so the recurrence path is closed and this is a measurement that has never existed, not a live bug. phase-051 is a different defect (uncommitted work, not ancestry) and does not cover it.
phases.goal: Add an executable check that fails when any `rbops: phase-NNN checkpoint` commit that is an ancestor of redblue main is not on a hand-maintained acknowledgement list, and record in the repository that the four existing ones carry unreviewed code and were not rewritten.
accept: a Rust test shells out to `git log --oneline main` in this repository, selects every commit whose subject matches `rbops: phase-[0-9]+ checkpoint`, and fails naming any SHA that is not in a checked-in acknowledgement list; an edge_* test feeds the selector a fixture history containing one unlisted SHA and asserts the check fails

run against redblue main as it stands the test passes, and the list it reports contains all four measured SHAs (7fdea15, 074c95e, 563a351, 286fccd) each with the reason it is tolerated - the list is data in the repository, not a comment
the same test counts `Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/rbops-wip/*'` commits on main (4 today) and prints the count, so a recurrence through a different resume path is visible rather than silent

a record in the test module states plainly that the four checkpoint commits carry unreviewed code, that published history was deliberately NOT rewritten, and that no force-push is attempted by this phase or any gate
on a shallow or absent history the test never reports a pass: it prints the reason it could not read the full history and fails, rather than treating a short log as a clean one
`cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added and no `#[ignore]`

phases.title: Land phase-041's work behind a commit, or take back its `.done`
phases.finding: phases/phase-041/.done exists and `git -C redblue log --oneline main --grep='phase-041 '` prints nothing. The work is sitting in the working tree: `git -C redblue status --porcelain` reports ` M src/parser.rs`, `A tests/text_split_join_test.rs`, `A phases/phase-041/REPORT.md`, `A phases/phase-041/FINDINGS.md`, and `git -C redblue diff --stat HEAD` totals 1800 insertions and 17 deletions, of which tests/text_split_join_test.rs is 1235 lines that no commit contains. The state store says the phase is complete, its REPORT describes a change that exists in no commit, and `cargo test` is green partly because 1235 lines of test code were never committed. The next `git checkout`, the next fresh CI clone, or the next phase that starts from a clean tree loses all of it. This is the defect class phase-051 names, but phase-051 names phase-022 specifically, and phase-022's work has since landed as 054e0d6 - so phase-051's finding no longer reproduces and this is the live instance.
phases.goal: Get phase-041's implementation onto redblue main behind a commit its own REPORT describes, so the gate is green from history rather than from an uncommitted working tree.
accept: `git -C redblue status --porcelain` prints nothing for `src/` or `tests/text_split_join_test.rs`, and `git -C redblue log --oneline main --grep='phase-041 '` prints at least one line

that commit's file list is compared BY NAME against the `What changed` table in phases/phase-041/REPORT.md - every file the table claims is in the commit and every file in the commit is in the table - and the comparison is asserted in the phase's own test, not left to review
the phase asserts `git status --porcelain` is EMPTY before running `cargo test --test text_split_join_test`, so a green run from a dirty tree cannot satisfy this criterion

the commit is single-parent on top of the previous main commit, and `git log --oneline main | grep -c checkpoint` is still 4 afterwards - this phase must not add checkpoint ancestry while fixing uncommitted work

the committed tests are audited against the AGENTS.md 3.2 edge matrix and any uncovered row is added: at minimum `split` on empty text, `split` with a separator absent from the text, and `join` on an empty list, each asserted to a named value
if the work cannot honestly be landed, `phases/phase-041/.done` is REMOVED and the phase ends with the phase re-runnable; it does not end with an uncommitted tree a second time
`cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added and no `#[ignore]`

phases.title: Make `items at N` and `length of X` real, or strike them from SPEC.md
phases.finding: SPEC.md:319 `set first to items at 0`, SPEC.md:320 `set last to items at -1` and SPEC.md:327 `set count to length of items` are written as working syntax under `### List Operations`. None of them works. Verified against the built binary: after `set items to [1,2,3]`, `set first to items at 0` gives `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'at'` (src/analyzer.rs:436) and `set count to length of items` gives `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'of'`. The cause is src/parser.rs:664-667 - the `_` arm of `parse_statement_inner` falls through to `parse_expression()` and wraps whatever it finds as `Statement::Expr`, so `set first to items at 0` is not a parse error at all, it is THREE statements: `set first to items`, `at`, `0`. Two tools then make it worse: `rb format` prints those three lines back (verified - `rb format` on that file emits `set first to items` / `at` / `0`), and `rb lint` reports no diagnostic at all on a file `rb` cannot run (verified - lint prints only `Unused variable: 'first'` and exits 0). No corpus, example or module program uses either form, so nothing else in the suite notices.
phases.goal: Either implement the two documented forms or correct SPEC.md, and stop the parser from silently turning an unconsumed line into stray expression statements.
accept: for each of SPEC.md:319, SPEC.md:320 and SPEC.md:327 individually: the program as written runs and prints the documented value, or SPEC.md is corrected and the correction is listed in REPORT.md - the three are decided one by one, not as a group

`set first to items at 0` is either the documented indexing form or a spanned ParserError, and it is never three statements: asserted by counting statements in the parsed `Program`, not by matching on the error text
`rb lint` reports at least one diagnostic for any file `rb` cannot run and none for a file it can; an edge_* test pairs each of the three forms above with its lint result and with its run result
`rb format` never changes a program's statement count: an edge_* test formats a program containing all three forms and asserts the formatted `Program`'s body length equals the source's
out-of-bounds stays a clean runtime error in whichever spelling survives - index `-1`, index `len` and index `999` each produce a spanned RuntimeError and never a panic, asserted per spelling
the corpus gains at least one program per surviving spelling so the differential harness exercises it on BOTH engines, and the engine answers are diffed rather than eyeballed
`cargo test` reports 0 failures, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added, and every file in `examples/` and `modules/` still exits 0

phases.title: Execute every ```redblue block in the five documents that define the language
phases.finding: 97 ```redblue blocks exist across the documents that define Redblue - SPEC.md 64, docs/GRAMMAR.md 9, PHILOSOPHY.md 9, HANDOUT.md 8, README.md 7 - and no test runs any of them. Every existing reference is a hand-quoted single example (tests/for_range_test.rs:2 cites SPEC.md:380-391, tests/formatter_test.rs:2008 cites SPEC.md:383). Measured this audit by extracting and running every block: 58 of 97 do not run, among them SPEC.md:319 and SPEC.md:327 (the phase-080 forms), SPEC.md:1068 (`LexerError: Unexpected character '\''` - Redblue has no single-quoted string), SPEC.md:1066 (`ParserError: Unexpected token Wait`, owned by phase-049) and HANDOUT.md:155 (`filter was called with arguments it cannot use`, owned by phase-077). Many of the 58 are fragments rather than defects - docs/GRAMMAR.md:526-532's example omits its `end` - so the first deliverable is an honest classification, NOT 58 features. The rotted examples are exactly the ones that cost an audit to find: `items at 0` sat in SPEC.md undetected until now.
phases.goal: Build the test that extracts and classifies every documentation code block, so a documentation promise cannot rot unnoticed, and turn the first true classification into a report a human can act on.
accept: a test extracts every ```redblue block from SPEC.md, README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, HANDOUT.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md, recording doc and line for each; the extracted count is asserted to be at least the 97 measured today, so deleting an example cannot silently shrink the suite

each block is classified into exactly one of three checked-in buckets - RUNS (executed, exit 0), FRAGMENT (a snippet, with a written reason such as 'elided end' for docs/GRAMMAR.md:526), or KNOWN-FAIL (doc:line plus the exact first line of stderr); a block in no bucket fails the test, so the lists cannot rot either
the buckets are DATA checked into the repository, matched by doc:line, not a permissive pattern re-derived at test time

REPORT.md states the true measured classification - how many RUNS, how many FRAGMENT, how many KNOWN-FAIL - and does NOT claim the 58 are 58 features; SPEC.md:319 and SPEC.md:327 are resolved by phase-080 before this phase is marked done
edge_* tests cover the extractor itself: a block with no closing fence, an empty block, a fenced block not tagged `redblue` (must be ignored), and a doc file that does not exist (must not panic)
the test asserts a failure is produced: a KNOWN-FAIL entry's recorded first stderr line must match what the block actually prints today, and mutating that line in the data fails the test
`cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added and no `#[ignore]`

phases.title: Make every place the project states what works, true
phases.finding: Five documents state what Redblue does and all five are wrong somewhere. SPEC.md:1068 writes `json.parse('{"name": "Alice"}')` with single quotes and the lexer rejects `'` - `LexerError: Unexpected character '\''`, raised at src/lexer.rs:506 - because Redblue has no single-quoted string. SPEC.md:1073 states 'There is no `formats` module' while HANDOUT.md:149 and HANDOUT.md:154 document `formats.parse_json` and `formats.to_json`. HANDOUT.md:155-157 document `list.map` and `list.filter`, and `list.filter` answers `filter was called with arguments it cannot use`; both names are listed as known gaps at tests/stdlib_module_docs_test.rs:259-261. README.md:237 lists `src/vm.rs` in the project structure and that file does not exist - it was renamed to `src/interpreter.rs`. README.md:279 still marks self-hosting 'in progress' although bootstrap/compiler.rb is 2854 lines and tests/bootstrap_selfhost_test.rs already asserts stage-2 and stage-3 byte-identical output (edge_stage2_is_byte_identical_on_every_corpus_program, edge_the_self_compiled_compiler_compiles_itself_byte_identical). Worst of all, tests/stdlib_module_docs_test.rs:270-274 exempts console_clear, time_unix, csv_parse, network_get and network_post as 'documented but not implemented', and ALL FIVE work at runtime: `console.clear()` clears, `time.unix("2024-01-01 00:00:00")` answers 1704067200, `csv.parse("a,b\n1,2")` answers `[[a, b], [1, 2]]`, `json.parse` answers a record. An exemption list that is stale in the PERMISSIVE direction stops testing things that work.
phases.goal: Correct every false statement in SPEC.md, README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, HANDOUT.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md and shrink the stale KNOWN_GAPS list, so no document claims a capability the binary lacks and no gate-supporting test exempts a working builtin.
accept: tests/stdlib_module_docs_test.rs no longer exempts console_clear, time_unix, csv_parse, network_get or network_post from the registry walk at tests/stdlib_module_docs_test.rs:277; all five are removed from KNOWN_GAPS and are now covered by that walk
every name removed from KNOWN_GAPS has a dedicated test that calls it and asserts its value - a name that merely stops being exempt is not enough, and the test names are listed in REPORT.md
the remaining KNOWN_GAPS entries each still carry their stated reason, and any that are now implemented are removed rather than left to excuse a later change

SPEC.md:1068 is corrected to Redblue's real string syntax, or single-quoted strings are implemented; either way the corrected example is in a RUNS or FRAGMENT bucket produced by phase-081 and a test executes it

HANDOUT.md:149 and HANDOUT.md:154 either drop `formats.*` (SPEC.md:1073 says the module does not exist) or SPEC.md is corrected, and REPORT.md names which document moved - the two must not disagree afterwards
README.md:237 names `src/interpreter.rs`, the file that exists, and README.md:279's self-hosting line reflects what bootstrap/compiler.rb and tests/bootstrap_selfhost_test.rs already do

edge_* tests cover the corrections: a doc example using single quotes, one naming `formats`, and one naming `list.filter` - each is either executed or listed with a reason, so a correction cannot be reverted silently
`cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added and no `#[ignore]`
